text.title: Django + Celery Background Jobs Procedure
text.summary: 8-step procedure applying the django-celery methodology end-to-end. Each step lists inputs, action, output, and optional decision gate.

step.name: inventory-tasks
step.action: List every task: name, trigger, payload shape, frequency, latency budget, failure consequence.

step.name: define-task-contract
step.input: task inventory + linked service + business id
step.action: Write task signature: (business_id, *, **kwargs) with an explicit dotted name= on the decorator; pick the idempotency strategy (idempotency_key | db_upsert | check_before_act | natural_key) and document the invariant in the docstring.
step.output: tasks.py stub with name + idempotency design

step.name: wire-dispatch
step.action: Replace bare .delay() with transaction.on_commit dispatch (or delay_on_commit on Celery 5.4+).
step.decision-gate: If dispatch is outside any transaction, document why in the call site.

step.name: add-retry-and-time-limits
step.input: task stub + latency budgets + failure consequence
step.action: Set autoretry_for + max_retries + retry_backoff + retry_jitter on the decorator; set soft_time_limit from p95 measurements and time_limit = soft + 30s.
step.output: tasks.py with a complete policy decorator

step.name: design-queue-topology
step.action: Assign tasks to named queues (emails, reports, webhooks); decide the worker pool and concurrency per queue and wire task_routes plus the worker `-Q` flags.
step.decision-gate: If queue count > worker count, consolidate; if one queue dominates, split.

step.name: configure-dlq
step.input: celery app config + per-task DLQ strategy + alerting endpoints
step.action: Define the DLQ in CELERY_TASK_QUEUES (or a failure-record table) and route on_failure to it; wire the PagerDuty/Slack alert on DLQ depth and growth.

step.name: test-idempotency
step.action: Call the task twice with the same business_key; assert single side-effect.

step.name: staging-soak
step.action: Run for ≥24h on staging at production traffic shape; observe DLQ, retry rate, queue depth, task age, p95 latency.
